territorial_scope.description: Applies to elections and campaign advertisements within the State of Georgia, with venue in any Georgia county where specified connections exist.

evidence.quote: Title 21 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated, relating to elections, is amended in Chapter 2

summary.short: Georgia bill HB 986 would make knowingly publishing materially deceptive audiovisual media within 90 days of an election, intended to deceive electors, a felony, and would require disclosure of AI-generated content in campaign advertisements. It would take effect on the Governor's approval. Registry status: failed.
summary.long: The bill would add Code Section 21-2-605 to Georgia's election code. Materially deceptive media means video, audio or still images that appear to depict a real individual's speech or conduct that did not occur and would appear authentic to a reasonable observer. Knowingly publishing, broadcasting, streaming or uploading such media within 90 days of an election, intending to deceive electors, would be a felony punishable by two to five years' imprisonment and a fine up to $50,000; soliciting such conduct would also be an offense. Satire, parody, artistic expression and bona fide journalism are excluded. The Attorney General would have concurrent prosecution jurisdiction, but prosecution would start only on a State Election Board recommendation. The depicted individual, the Attorney General or an injured candidate could seek injunctive relief. The State Election Board would publish findings of completed investigations. A new Article 21-5-90 et seq. would allow AI-generated content in campaign advertisements only if disclosed, with prescribed size and duration requirements; violations would carry a fine of at least $10,000. The Act would take effect on the Governor's approval or on becoming law without approval.

notes: The document is the bill text only; it contains no enactment or status information. Registry metadata gives status failed and stage dead. Internal inconsistencies: 'materially deceptive media' (21-2-605(a)(2)) and 'AI generated media' (21-5-90(1)) are defined separately with different elements, and 21-5-91 permits AI-generated content 'notwithstanding' 21-2-605 if disclosed. 21-2-605(b)(3) refers to 'such referendum' although the offence is otherwise framed around elections. The fine regimes differ: 21-5-93(a) sets a $10,000 minimum under 21-5-6, while 21-2-605(e) sets a felony fine up to $50,000. Stray numbers in the text (e.g., 24, 62, 78, 98, 101, 159) look like line-number artefacts and were ignored.

thresholds.variable_text: within 90 days of an election (window for the materially deceptive media offense)
thresholds.measurement: Time window relative to an election date; the text says 'within' and does not specify before, after or either side. Not stated who measures it.
thresholds.consequence: Publishing, broadcasting, streaming or uploading materially deceptive media is an offense under subsection (b) only when done within this window.
thresholds.conditions: Also requires knowledge of falsity, intent to deceive electors, and one of the purposes listed in subsection (b)(1) to (3).
